title: Fixed-width binary increment in linear time
statement: There are a finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet and a constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, on every Boolean input word $x$, $M$ outputs the fixed-width binary increment of $x$, read least-significant bit first, and halts within $c(|x|+1)$ steps; when incrementing overflows, the output is the empty word.
replaced:
There exist a finite Turing machine $M$ and a constant $c$ such that $M$
computes, within $c\,(n+1)$ steps on inputs of length $n$, the fixed-width
binary successor of its input read least-significant bit first, with empty
output on overflow (an all-ones input).
